title: Drift-Aware Multimodal User Representation Learning via Multi-Scale Temporal Modeling and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
claim: A multi-scale temporal backbone feeds a sparse expert adapter whose gated routing yields one representation for several downstream tasks.
layout: 2 dashed modules, left-to-right, input to dual task heads, with loss annotations
description: A horizontal left-to-right pipeline. On the left, a gray input box holds a profile icon and a timeline of interaction sequences with document and image icons. These feed a blue trapezoid Multi-modal Encoder. The output splits into three branches (static preference, short-term, long-term). Each branch goes through an MLP, LSTM or Transformer. All three sit inside a blue dashed panel (a) labeled Backbone Network. Each branch yields a small blue grid vector. The three vectors are fused into a gray vector z_u. This enters a peach dashed panel (b), the MoE Interest Adapter. Inside, a gating network produces weights α1..αk for experts A1..Ak, followed by norm, TopK and a multiplication node. A soft-max step gives h_u. The output splits into two heads, φ_cls and φ_rec. Gray loss boxes L_cls and L_rec connect to these heads with dashed arrows.
caption: Algorithm Overview.
abstract: Understanding user preferences from noisy and temporally evolving social media behaviors is fundamentally challenging due to interest drift, where user preferences shift across time and exhibit both multi-scale temporal patterns and diverse co-existing interests. To address this, we propose DUMoE, a unified framework for drift-aware multimodal user representation learning. Our model consists of (i) a temporal dynamics-aware backbone that captures and integrates static profiles, short-term behavioral signals, and long-term dependencies into a coherent representation, and (ii) a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) interest adapter that disentangles multiple latent interests via expert specialization and adaptive routing. Each expert models a distinct interest subspace, while a gating network dynamically selects and aggregates a sparse subset of relevant experts for each user. To enable stable and effective optimization, we further introduce a three-stage training strategy that decouples backbone learning, expert specialization, and gating optimization. Extensive experiments on real-world social media datasets show that DUMoE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both user interest prediction and interaction prediction tasks.Code is available at https://github.com/idvxlab/DUMoE.
